# A list-plugin arm asserts the whole process logged nothing, so another spec's watchdog reds it

## Context

Promoted from a `defect-note` (2026-09-16) after it reddened four CI jobs across three branches that touch neither `list/` nor the vdom engine:

| job | branch | shape |
|---|---|---|
| 104744290891 | `grace/18764-grid-native-cell-editing` | `1 flaky · 31 skipped · 4156 passed`, exit 1 |
| 104756364740 | `grace/18776-domaccess-stub-restore` | same |
| 104757342426 | same branch as the first, rerun | same |
| 104769387625 | `grace/18771-grid-renderer-scope` | `2 flaky`, this arm plus the one #18785 fixed |

The arm is `Neo.list.plugin.Animate — measured row height › the guard admits itemHeight null with measureItemHeight, and refuses it without` (`test/playwright/unit/list/animatePlugin.spec.mjs:551`). It fails at `:560`, `expect(errors).toEqual([])`, and the array holds:

```
vdom update wedged: "my-test-component" has been in-flight for over 5000ms.
Its reply was likely lost — the component will not update again…
```

`my-test-component` is not this spec's. It is created by `test/playwright/unit/functional/HtmlTemplateComponent.spec.mjs:108`.

**The gate is deliberate and not the defect.** `playwright.config.unit.mjs:28` sets `failOnFlakyTests: isCI` with `retries: 2`, so a retry-passing arm reds the job on purpose. The leaf is the arm.

## The Problem

The arm captures the process's `console.error` and then asserts that *nothing at all* was logged:

```js
const errors = [], prior = console.error;

console.error = (...args) => errors.push(String(args[0]));

try {
    const {list} = await createFixture(measuredConfig());
    expect(errors).toEqual([]);                       // ← :560, any process log fails here
```

One Playwright worker runs many spec files in one process, and `VDomUpdate`'s wedge watchdog is a 5-second `setTimeout` armed by whichever component was updating when it started. So a watchdog armed by an earlier spec file fires inside this arm's capture window and is attributed to it. The arm asks "did the guard complain?" and is answered "did anything in this process log an error in the last few milliseconds?".

That is the same class as #18785 (an arm asserting `DragCoordinator.sortZones` is empty while other specs share the process), fixed by narrowing the assertion to the arm's own target.

**What this ticket does not claim.** Whether that watchdog *should* fire — whether some component really does leave an in-flight update behind — is a separate question, broadcast as its own defect-note and not owned here. Fixing the arm does not silence the watchdog: it keeps logging, for whoever owns it.

## The Architectural Reality

| surface | today |
|---|---|
| `test/playwright/unit/list/animatePlugin.spec.mjs:551-569` | captures `console.error` process-wide; asserts emptiness, then asserts one message mentions `measureItemHeight` |
| `src/manager/VDomUpdate.mjs:121-137` | `watchdogThreshold = 5000` and `watchdogTimerMap`; the timer is armed per in-flight update and cleared by `unregisterInFlightUpdate` |
| `test/playwright/unit/functional/HtmlTemplateComponent.spec.mjs:108` | creates `my-test-component`, the id the leaked message names |
| `test/playwright/playwright.config.unit.mjs:28` | `failOnFlakyTests: isCI`, `retries: 2` — deliberate, per @neo-opus-ada's correction |
| #18785 / PR #18786 | the same class, one arm over, already fixed by scoping the assertion |

## The Fix

Scope the arm to its own subject. It exists to prove two things about the `measureItemHeight` guard — that a valid config draws no complaint, and that an invalid one draws exactly one — so both assertions read the messages the guard produces rather than the process's log:

- keep every captured message, but assert over the subset this arm is about (the guard's own text), so an unrelated process log neither passes nor fails it;
- leave the capture/restore in `try/finally` as it is;
- state in one line why the filter exists, so the next reader does not "simplify" it back to `toEqual([])`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — the arm fails when the guard misbehaves: with `measureItemHeight` accepted for a config it must refuse, or refused for one it must admit, the assertions still red (its original contract is intact).
- [ ] **AC-2** — the arm passes when an unrelated `console.error` is emitted inside its window; an injected message proves it, and removing the filter makes that injection red again.
- [ ] **AC-3** — the file's other arms are unchanged and green.
- [ ] **AC-4** — the unit tier passes locally, and `list/animatePlugin.spec.mjs` paired with `functional/HtmlTemplateComponent.spec.mjs` in one worker stays green.

## Out of Scope

- Whether a component leaves an in-flight update behind for the watchdog to find. Separate defect-note, unowned; this ticket makes the arm honest, not the engine quiet.
- `failOnFlakyTests` / `retries`: deliberate policy (`playwright.config.unit.mjs:28`), and weakening it would hide exactly this kind of finding.
- The other flaky arm in the same jobs: #18785, already fixed.

## Avoided Traps

- **Re-running until green.** Four jobs across three branches, each costing a 2-minute rerun, is the cost of treating this as weather.
- **Silencing the watchdog** or lowering its threshold: it is the only thing that names a lost reply, and it is right to be loud.
- **Asserting emptiness "but ignoring known messages" by string-blacklist.** A blacklist grows with every new unrelated logger; asking about the guard's own output does not.
